summary.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated SSSG rose to 14.4% (Q3: 8.2%) with dine-in volumes up ~43%, and management targets 9-10% pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin in FY27.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's strongest operating quarter in recent history, with consolidated revenue of INR360 crores (+23.1% YoY) and every segment and channel growing at double-digit rates. Growth was entirely volume-led with no price increase in Q4, while gross margin fell about 300 bps YoY to 65.5% due to segment mix, value campaigns in weaker dayparts and Middle East input inflation. Management says gross margin bottomed in February 2026 and recovered about 100 bps in March and April. Net debt was about INR100-102 crores, and FY27 guidance includes 40 new restaurants, around INR140 crores of capex and a 9-10% pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Barbeque Nation India
segments.commentary: Q4 SSSG 16.7% (Q3: 8.3%) and dine-in volume +47% YoY; more than 60% of dine-in transactions now via own digital channels (Q3: 53%). Lower per-cover spend than other segments diluted average realisation.

segments.name: Barbeque Nation International
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +27.5% YoY, SSSG 5.5%, dine-in volume ~+27%; pre-Ind AS restaurant operating margin ~24.4%. Added 4 restaurants in FY26 (most ever); 3 under construction in Middle East and Southeast Asia. Two of ~8 restaurants (Bahrain, Dubai) impacted by West Asia crisis.

segments.name: Premium CDR (Salt and Toscano)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +23.3% YoY, SSSG 7%, dine-in volume ~+27%. Network grew from 30 to 42 restaurants in FY26; mature store pre-Ind AS ROM 18.4% in Q4 and 20.1% for FY26, while new-store cohort margins compressed in newer markets (Mumbai, Delhi).

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin target of 9-10%, with a path to double-digit margins thereafter; management clarified this is a full-year figure, not an exit rate.

FY27 SSSG internal aim: mid-single-digit to double-digit on a normalised base; management says it internally aims to cross double-digit full-year SSSG, and blended premium CDR plus International SSSG at early double-digit.
H1 FY27 SSSG expected to hold at Q4 levels, with possible slight improvement in Q1; management said Q1 and Q2 momentum is continuing.

Gross margin recovery of 100-150 bps in FY27 over Q4 levels, targeting a 67-68% medium-term band; mature ROM expected to rise from ~16% (H2 FY26 basis) to 17-18%; new-store drag 1.5-1.8%; consolidated ROM 15.5-16.5%.
Back-end cost to fall from 7.1% to ~6.5% of revenue in FY27 and ~6% over the longer term.
Plan to open 40 new restaurants in FY27 (network 300+ by end FY27) and reach 400-425 restaurants by FY30; 11 restaurants under construction to open in Q1-Q2 FY27.

FY27 capex of ~INR140 crores (30 India restaurants at ~INR2.5 crores, 5 International at ~INR6 crores, 5 premium CDR at ~INR3 crores, ~INR20 crores maintenance); expansion to be funded mainly from internal accruals, with net debt expected to stay flat.
Management said FY27 full-year revenue growth of 22-25% is reasonable if SSSG is double-digit and store expansion is 12-13% (answered 'on a full year basis, yes').
capex_capacity: FY26: 35 new restaurants added (14 in Q4), taking network to 262; 32 net additions versus 14 net in the prior two years combined.
FY27 plan: 40 new restaurants (~15% expansion), with 11 under construction and further advanced commercial discussions; FY28 target of 100-125 restaurants over three years (40-45 per year).
Capex plan FY27 ~INR140 crores, of which ~INR120 crores for new stores; International 5 stores at ~INR6 crores each; India 30 stores at ~INR2.5 crores; premium CDR 5 stores at ~INR3 crores.

Management says the 4-session-per-day model allows 3-4 table turns; a 100-seat restaurant can do ~300 covers/day, and peak restaurants do INR12-13 crores (India) and INR11-12 crores (Salt and Toscano).
demand_pricing: Approximately 90% of dine-in volume comes from captive channels (app, website, in-house reservation centre, walk-ins); monthly active users on app and website crossed 1.2 million, up 51% YoY.

Growth was volume-led: Q4 had no price increase. Management says it can recover INR15-20 net realisation per cover through base pricing, group offers and beverage mix, and is pulling back marginally on some campaign offers to full price.

Company-level AOV fell ~14-15% YoY due to mix (higher Barbeque India covers, weaker dayparts); management expects this to persist for two more quarters, then settle at levels similar to the last two quarters.
Delivery revenue grew ~32% YoY, led entirely by transaction growth.
Management is not pursuing discount-led growth that compromises unit economics; no new brand categories or acquisitions planned in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is double-digit SSSG for FY27 achievable given the cautious tone on H2 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects early double-digit SSSG comfortably and that the internal aim is to cross double-digit full-year SSSG, while declining to give formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 9-10% margin target be achieved from the current base, and is the 100-150 bps gross margin recovery net of inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 67-68% gross margin range is after inflation; gross margin gap to FY25 peak of 68.5% is now ~3 pp and expected to narrow to ~1-1.5 pp. Gross margin rose in March and April despite LPG price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q4 new-store drag on margins persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 new-store drag was 180 bps (vs 120 bps in Q4 FY25) as Q4 was the heaviest opening quarter; management expects drag to narrow as the cohort matures over 12-24 months, stabilising at 1.5-1.8%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did premium CDR margins fall sharply from Q3 to Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to new restaurants (4 opened in Q4), seasonality (December peak in Q3), one-time setup and liquor costs, and newer markets (Mumbai, Delhi) that take time to build up; mature cohort margins are fine.

qa_highlights.question: How will store expansion avoid the closures seen in FY23?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some Tier 2/3 stores were closed in FY23 but its current operating model works in those markets; FY27 plan of 40 stores is ~15% of the base and comparable to the 35 added in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for International given Middle East disruption and currency effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Two of ~8 restaurants (Bahrain, Dubai) are impacted; both improved month-on-month in April and May. No new Middle East sites reviewed in the last three months; focus is on Southeast Asia.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company's per-restaurant revenue and peak capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peak-day capacity is not a constraint: a 4-session day at 100 seats gives 400 covers, about INR9 crores a month at INR750 per cover, and the company will open nearby stores 5-7 km apart when demand grows.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery (100-150 bps) depends on procurement, scale and selective realisation, against input inflation (LPG, utilities, Middle East) and continued value campaigns in weaker dayparts.
Tougher comparison base in H2 FY27 after strong Q3 and Q4 FY26 SSSG (8.2% and 14.4%); management says the planning factors this in.
New-store cohort drag (180 bps in Q4 FY26) and premium CDR margin compression in new markets (Mumbai, Delhi) could delay the mature ROM path.
Middle East (Bahrain, Dubai) and currency headwinds on International; management says it is not signing new sites there for now.
Store-expansion execution (40 stores in FY27, 100-125 over three years) given closures in FY23 Tier 2/3 markets; back-end cost must fall from 7.1% to 6.5% of revenue.
Monitor Q1 FY27 SSSG and gross margin trend, and any change to internal targets flagged for the Q1 results.
key_quotes: Q4 FY'26 has been the strongest operating quarter in our recent history.
I would believe that we would be able to comfortably deliver an early double-digit same-store sales growth. It is just that I'm on the side of caution to give guidance.
We are not chasing discount-led growth that comprises unit economics.
Our internal aim is to take pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin to 9% to 10% in FY'27 with a path towards double-digit margins going forward.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand momentum and the volume-led recovery, citing two consecutive quarters of strong SSSG and every segment growing double-digit. Cautious on forward guidance: management declined to give formal FY27 SSSG guidance, offering "early double-digit" only as a comfortable expectation and an internal aim, and stressed that the H2 comparison base will be tougher.

FY28 target of 100-125 restaurants over three years (40-45 per year)
